{{Short description|Region underneath a graph}}
[[File:Hypograph en.svg|alt=|right|thumb|upright=1.5|Hypograph of a function]]
In [[mathematics]], the '''hypograph''' or '''subgraph''' of a [[function (mathematics)|function]] <math>f:\R^{n}\rightarrow \R</math> is the [[Set (mathematics)|set]] of points lying on or below its [[Graph of a function|graph]]. 
A related definition is that of such a function's [[Epigraph (mathematics)|epigraph]], which is the set of points on or above the function's graph. 

The [[domain of a function|domain]] (rather than the [[codomain]]) of the function is not particularly important for this definition; it can be an arbitrary set<ref name="AliprantisBorder2007" /> instead of <math>\mathbb{R}^n</math>.

== Definition ==

The definition of the hypograph was inspired by that of the [[graph of a function]], where the {{em|'''graph'''}} of <math>f : X \to Y</math> is defined to be the set 

:<math>\operatorname{graph} f := \left\{ (x, y) \in X \times Y ~:~ y = f(x) \right\}.</math>

The {{em|'''hypograph'''}} or {{em|'''subgraph'''}} of a function <math>f : X \to [-\infty, \infty]</math> valued in the [[Extended real number line|extended real numbers]] <math>[-\infty, \infty] = \mathbb{R} \cup \{ \pm \infty \}</math> is the set{{sfn|Rockafellar|Wets|2009|pp=1-37}}

:<math>
\begin{alignat}{4}
\operatorname{hyp} f 
&= \left\{ (x, r) \in X \times \mathbb{R} ~:~ r \leq f(x) \right\} \\
&= \left[ f^{-1}(\infty) \times \mathbb{R} \right] \cup \bigcup_{x \in f^{-1}(\mathbb{R})} (\{ x \} \times (-\infty, f(x)]).
\end{alignat}
</math>

Similarly, the set of points on or above the function is its [[Epigraph (mathematics)|epigraph]]. 
{{anchor|Strict hypograph}}
The {{em|'''strict hypograph'''}} is the hypograph with the graph removed:

:<math>
\begin{alignat}{4}
\operatorname{hyp}_S f 
&= \left\{ (x, r) \in X \times \mathbb{R} ~:~ r < f(x) \right\} \\
&= \operatorname{hyp} f \setminus \operatorname{graph} f \\
&= \bigcup_{x \in X} (\{ x \} \times (-\infty, f(x))).
\end{alignat}
</math>

Despite the fact that <math>f</math> might take one (or both) of <math>\pm \infty</math> as a value (in which case its graph would {{em|not}} be a subset of <math>X \times \mathbb{R}</math>), the hypograph of <math>f</math> is nevertheless defined to be a subset of <math>X \times \mathbb{R}</math> rather than of <math>X \times [-\infty, \infty].</math>

== Properties ==

The hypograph of a function <math>f</math> is [[Empty set|empty]] if and only if <math>f</math> is identically equal to negative infinity.

A function is [[Concave function|concave]] if and only if its hypograph is a [[convex set]]. The hypograph of a real [[affine function]] <math>g : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}</math> is a [[Half-space (geometry)|halfspace]] in <math>\mathbb{R}^{n+1}.</math> 

A function is [[Semi-continuity|upper semicontinuous]] if and only if its hypograph is [[Closed set|closed]].
